title: Prove a complete four-width criterion for affine-quadratic native identities
body:
An identity between native monomial circuits can pass small tensor widths and fail later. This PR proves a complete criterion for fixed binary affine maps with quadratic Gaussian phases: on `n >= 1` axes, equality at **2n+4, 2n+5, 2n+6 and 2n+7** is equivalent to equality at **every positive tensor width**. Scalar coefficients stay outside tensor powers, and the endpoint includes every arbitrary dirty input and returned role.

The [proof](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/research/native-tensor-cutoff/PROOF.md) constructs a nonzero basis entry for every failed identity, with its input/output addresses encoded in O(n²) bits. It also proves exact phase-residue kernel stabilization by width 2n+4. For this monomial group, the linear bound replaces the retained general `|G/Z|-1` sufficient bound. Four widths are necessary because each central phase residue can hide a different error; the value 2n+4 is not claimed to be the least cutoff.

Start with the [contributor guide](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/docs/research/native-tensor-cutoff.md), [replay receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/research/native-tensor-cutoff/RESULT.json), [source pins](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/research/native-tensor-cutoff/SOURCE-PINS.json), and [source/related-work manifest](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/research/native-tensor-cutoff/SOURCES.json).

This is an enabling proof and reusable exact checker. **The complete κ remains 60403/20000000.** The [selected record](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/certificates/selected-result.json) and all physical supplier, ownership, compiler, precision/tape and outer recovery obligations remain unchanged. Hadamard operators, arbitrary width-dependent programs, nonlinear leaves, external aliases and rectangular types are outside this theorem.

The package includes three useful boundaries:

- A rank-projector family vanishes at every width below n and is nonzero at n. The supplied nine-axis example passes all widths 1 through 8.
- Equality is coNP-complete even with five arbitrary dirty roles, only reversible operations, and commuting native sign generators. The proof gives an explicit reduction using Barrington's classical width-five construction and a five-step controlled swap. Sparse circuit expansion can be exponential; no fast general solver is claimed.
- The actual event8814 nine-axis recipe satisfies a complete native conjugation identity. Omitting its global sign passes the even-width probes but fails at a generated width-25 witness, with discrepancy -2. This binds the supplied recipe bytes and conventions, not the full dispatcher-to-chart chain or production packet.

The [producer](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/research/native-tensor-cutoff/native_identity.py) compares canonical native coefficients; it does not build the four tensor matrices. The [separate checker](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/research/native-tensor-cutoff/check_certificate.py) uses direct Boolean-polynomial substitution for positive claims and literal basis execution for negative claims. It imports no producer or native-algebra code. Exact rational arithmetic, Python and instruction semantics are shared trust.

Validation ran on macOS with CPython 3.12.14 and no third-party dependencies:

```sh
python3 -I -W error -B research/native-tensor-cutoff/verify.py
python3 -I -O -W error -B research/native-tensor-cutoff/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/native-tensor-cutoff/audit_mutations.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/native-tensor-cutoff
```

The first two commands return the same JSON with status `PASS_NATIVE_TENSOR_CUTOFF`. The mutation audit returns `PASS_NATIVE_CUTOFF_MUTATIONS`; the registered runner ends with `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/native-tensor-cutoff outcome=completed`.

The replay covers 33,866 symmetric binary matrices, 2,192 phase characters, 100 larger character cases through 73 axes, 1,152 native composition pairs, 120 complete circuits, 11,760 dirty-input basis cases, 4,444 below-rank projector cases, 80 CNF formulas on 992 assignments, 480 reversible branch pairs, all 512 source addresses, five committed certificates and 37 rejection controls. Four private-copy mathematical mutations fail in both Python modes; their [receipt](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/research/native-tensor-cutoff/MUTATIONS.json) names the semantic rejection checks. Committed-byte checks, official export integrity, and normal/optimized Git-free replays in a fresh read-only export also pass. Finite checks support the written uniform proof; they do not replace it.

No selected cold replay, Lean, Docker, independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed. The full-history ancestry check was omitted in this shallow checkout; the recorded source objects and retained bytes were checked. Hosted CI is reported separately by GitHub.

Scientific base: current canonical main `7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56`, priority revision 7. All six consumed source exports are pinned to that commit; no pending PR head is imported. The final advisory overlap snapshot covers 316 open PRs and 4,648 Discussion records, with complete remote pagination. Related source proofs were read separately. Arbitrary historical diffs and unpublished work are outside that coverage. Coordination is in [Discussion #5354](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/5354).

Douglas Colkitt's construction and the retained authors keep the credit in the [unchanged notice](https://github.com/aliromman/integer-mult-bounds/blob/18354f41de4dc7bfda4692e814cf1d91a6d619ef/research/native-tensor-cutoff/source/NOTICE.md).

The [exact recipe](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/complex-segment-boundary/RIGHT-RECIPE.json) is consumed without claiming their remaining caller obligations.

The [general separation proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/two-full-retained-helper-ceiling/science/PROOF.md) and [binary-stream proof](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/blob/7c472563474e60185e6ca101a17622133d047e56/research/binary-stream-faithfulness/PROOF.md) are comparisons, not imported verifiers.
- @zxv in [PR #5235](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5235) and @krzysztofwojt in [PR #5262](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5262) supply the related independent-operator and named-inverse certificate interfaces. The native finite-order and phase relations here require a different grammar.

Lempel's binary Gram factorization, finite Fourier inversion, Burnside-Brauer tensor generation, Pauli conjugation, SAT completeness and Barrington's permutation programs are classical and cited in the proof. No global literature priority is claimed. New work by Ali Romman with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0. The proof and guide leave concrete next questions about the least cutoff, nonmonomial Cliffords and further source-bound adapters.
